paper.title: Advances and Challenges in Foundation Agents: From Brain-Inspired Intelligence to Evolutionary, Collaborative, and Safe Systems

summary.one_sentence: This survey reframes agents as foundation-agent systems with brain-inspired modules, self-evolution, multi-agent collaboration, and safety as coequal design axes.
summary.thesis: The paper's contribution is a broad 2025 synthesis: move beyond LLM-as-controller toward modular agents with perception, cognition, action, memory, world models, reward/goals, emotion-like state, adaptive self-enhancement, social coordination, and safety mechanisms.
summary.why_it_matters: For agent infrastructure, this is a roadmap paper. It shows which state, learning, coordination, and safety surfaces future agent runtimes will have to expose and govern.

prior_state: Earlier LLM-agent taxonomies often centered on prompting, memory, tools, and applications.
2024-2025 work expanded the agent field into multimodal perception, self-improvement, reinforcement learning, world models, scientific agents, and multi-agent societies.
Agent systems increasingly need continuous improvement, collaboration, and safety properties rather than one-shot task execution.
The field lacked a single synthesis that connected brain-inspired modular design with evolutionary, collaborative, and safe systems.
problem.key_gap: The survey asks how to organize foundation agents as modular, adaptive, collaborative, and safe systems rather than isolated LLM wrappers.
assumptions: Brain-inspired functional modules can be useful as a design and gap-analysis framework for intelligent agents.
Foundation agents require a perception-cognition-action loop with internal state that changes over time.
Self-enhancement and multi-agent collaboration are central research directions, not optional add-ons.
Safety must cover intrinsic model risks and extrinsic deployment risks across agent modules and societies.

concepts.name: Foundation agent
concepts.definition: A general-purpose intelligent agent built around modular perception, cognition, action, internal state, adaptation, collaboration, and safety.

concepts.name: Perception-cognition-action loop
concepts.definition: A loop in which observations feed perception, cognition updates internal state and reasons, and actions affect the world.

concepts.name: Mental state
concepts.definition: The agent's evolving internal state, including memory, world model, goals, reward/learning signals, and emotion-like state.

concepts.name: World model
concepts.definition: A component that represents or simulates environmental dynamics, possible futures, and the consequences of actions.

concepts.name: Self-enhancement
concepts.definition: Mechanisms by which an agent autonomously improves capabilities, adapts to environments, or performs continual learning and optimization.

concepts.name: Collaborative and evolutionary systems
concepts.definition: Multi-agent settings where agents interact, cooperate, compete, specialize, or evolve collective behavior.

concepts.name: Safe and beneficial agents
concepts.definition: The design goal of mitigating intrinsic and extrinsic risks, including security threats, alignment failures, robustness gaps, and societal harm.

method.core_idea: Synthesize foundation-agent research into four connected layers: modular brain-inspired components, self-enhancement, collaborative/evolutionary multi-agent systems, and safety.
action_grammar: perception: multimodal sensing and observation intake.
cognition: learning, reasoning, planning, decision-making, and internal state update.
memory: persistent and working state used for continuity and retrieval.
world model: predictive or simulator-like representation of environment dynamics.
goal/reward: objectives and feedback signals that shape learning and behavior.
emotion-like state: internal modulatory signals inspired by human affect and motivation.
action: external or internal action produced by reasoning.
self-evolution: optimization, continual learning, and automated improvement.
collaboration: multi-agent interaction, cooperation, and societal structures.
safety: intrinsic/extrinsic threats, ethics, robustness, and mitigation strategies.
steps: Define foundation agents as modular intelligent systems rather than just LLM-driven applications.
Map core agent components to brain-inspired functional analogies.
Survey cognition, memory, perception, world models, action, reward, and emotion-like systems.
Survey self-enhancement and adaptive evolution mechanisms for autonomous improvement.
Survey collaborative and evolutionary multi-agent systems and their collective intelligence.
Survey safety, security, alignment, robustness, and mitigation strategies for trustworthy deployment.
Use the modular view to expose open challenges and research gaps.
method.pseudocode:
mental_state = {
  memory,
  world_model,
  goals,
  reward_signals,
  emotion_like_state
}

while agent_is_active:
  observation = perceive(environment)
  mental_state = learn(mental_state, previous_action, observation)
  action = reason_and_plan(mental_state)
  environment = execute(action)

# Foundation-agent infrastructure has to make this loop inspectable, controllable, and safe.

claims.statement: The survey frames foundation agents with a modular, brain-inspired architecture integrating cognitive, perceptual, and operational modules.
caveats: The brain mapping is a design analogy and organizing framework, not a claim of biological equivalence.

claims.statement: Core components include cognition, memory, perception, world models, action, reward, and emotion-like systems.
claims.scope: Abstract and companion repository table of contents.
caveats: Some components are more mature than others; the survey is intentionally broad.

claims.statement: The paper emphasizes a perception-cognition-action loop with evolving internal state rather than a stateless prompt-response model.
caveats: The review uses external summaries for the detailed formal loop because the ar5iv HTML was unavailable.

claims.statement: Self-enhancement and adaptive evolution are treated as central mechanisms for agents that refine capabilities and adapt to dynamic environments.
caveats: Autonomous self-improvement remains a research direction with unresolved reliability and safety constraints.

claims.statement: The survey treats collaborative and evolutionary multi-agent systems as a major axis, focusing on collective intelligence, cooperation, and societal structures.
caveats: Collective behavior can also amplify coordination failures and safety risks.

claims.statement: The survey explicitly places safe and beneficial AI alongside agent architecture, covering intrinsic and extrinsic security threats, ethical alignment, robustness, and mitigation.
caveats: A survey can identify safety categories, but production safety requires concrete mechanisms, audits, and enforcement layers.

claims.statement: For this project, the paper suggests that future review schemas should track not only memory/tools/planning, but also world models, reward signals, self-evolution, multi-agent coordination, and safety controls.
caveats: This is a reviewer inference from the survey's scope and the existing review database design.

evidence.result: The survey frames intelligent agents within a modular, brain-inspired architecture that integrates cognitive science, neuroscience, and computational research.

agent_infra_takeaways: The paper is useful as a forward-looking schema stress test: it adds world models, reward/goals, emotion-like state, and self-evolution to the usual memory/tool/planning checklist.
Foundation-agent infrastructure needs inspectable internal state, not just logs of external tool calls.
World models and reward signals create new audit surfaces because they can shape future behavior without an obvious immediate tool call.
Self-evolving agents need versioning, rollback, evaluation gates, and provenance for every optimization step.
Collaborative agent systems need protocol-level safety, coordination invariants, and containment of cross-agent error propagation.
The safety axis reinforces the repo's runtime framing: capability, learning, and collaboration are only useful if paired with enforceable trust boundaries.
caveats: This is a very broad 2025 survey/book, not a single empirical contribution.
The brain-inspired framing is useful for gap analysis but can overstate biological analogy if read too literally.
The detailed ar5iv HTML was unavailable during this review, so the review relies on the arXiv abstract plus companion project materials and accessible summaries.
Some sections describe aspirational research directions rather than mature production patterns.
Because the paper was revised after initial submission, exact internal sectioning may change across versions.
